claim: Antibiotics from few culturable microorganisms have saved millions of lives since the 20th century.
source: Antibiotics from few culturable microorganisms have saved millions of lives since the 20th century.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific and historical fact about the impact of antibiotics.

claim: With resistance formation, antibiotic compounds become increasingly ineffective.
source: But with resistance formation, these compounds become increasingly ineffective, while the majority of microbial and with that chemical compound diversity remains inaccessible for cultivation and exploration.
evidence: This reflects established knowledge about antibiotic resistance.

claim: The majority of microbial and chemical compound diversity remains inaccessible for cultivation and exploration.
source: But with resistance formation, these compounds become increasingly ineffective, while the majority of microbial and with that chemical compound diversity remains inaccessible for cultivation and exploration.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in microbiology about the 'great plate count anomaly'.

claim: Culturing recalcitrant bacteria is a stochastic process.
source: Culturing recalcitrant bacteria is a stochastic process.
evidence: This is supported by established understanding of bacterial cultivation challenges.

claim: Conventional cultivation methods are limited to low throughput.
source: But conventional methods are limited to low throughput.
evidence: This is a known limitation of traditional microbiological methods.

claim: Highly parallelized in-droplet cultivation starting from single cells results in the cultivation of yet uncultured species.
source: We demonstrate that highly parallelized in-droplet cultivation starting from single cells results in the cultivation of yet uncultured species and a significantly higher bacterial diversity than standard agar plate cultivation.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, including 16S rRNA sequencing and isolation results.

claim: Highly parallelized in-droplet cultivation results in significantly higher bacterial diversity than standard agar plate cultivation.
source: We demonstrate that highly parallelized in-droplet cultivation starting from single cells results in the cultivation of yet uncultured species and a significantly higher bacterial diversity than standard agar plate cultivation.
evidence: This is supported by alpha diversity indices and community composition data shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Strains able to inhibit intact reporter strains were isolated from the droplet system.
source: Strains able to inhibit intact reporter strains were isolated from the system.
evidence: This is supported by the screening experiments and isolation of antibiotic-producing strains described in the Results section.

claim: A variety of antimicrobial compounds were detected for a selected potent antibiotic producer.
source: A variety of antimicrobial compounds were detected for a selected potent antibiotic producer.
evidence: This is supported by LC-HRMS data showing bacillaenes and surfactins in Figure 7.

claim: The microbial diversity in environmental habitats provides a rich resource for medically relevant substances.
source: The microbial diversity in environmental habitats provides a rich resource for medically relevant substances (Moloney, 2016), and fortunately, it is far from being exhaustively mapped (Lloyd et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Microbial diversity in environmental habitats is far from being exhaustively mapped.
source: The microbial diversity in environmental habitats provides a rich resource for medically relevant substances (Moloney, 2016), and fortunately, it is far from being exhaustively mapped (Lloyd et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lloyd et al., 2018.

claim: Only 1–15% of the bacterial diversity are cultivable under standard laboratory conditions.
source: Only 1–15% of the bacterial diversity are cultivable under standard laboratory conditions (Lok, 2015), which promises further revolutionizing compounds to be discovered in the remaining unexplored majority.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lok, 2015.

claim: The remaining unexplored bacterial diversity promises further revolutionizing compounds to be discovered.
source: Only 1–15% of the bacterial diversity are cultivable under standard laboratory conditions (Lok, 2015), which promises further revolutionizing compounds to be discovered in the remaining unexplored majority.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the cited fact about uncultivable diversity.

claim: Initial continuous propagation of cultures is mandatory to study the chemical and biological characteristics of their respective natural products.
source: Initial continuous propagation of cultures is mandatory to study the chemical and biological characteristics of their respective natural products.
evidence: This is established knowledge in microbiology and natural product research.

claim: The concentration and composition of media have been adapted for a large number of oligotrophic uncultured species.
source: For instance, the concentration and composition of media have been adapted for a large number of oligotrophic uncultured species (Olsen and Bakken, 1987; Janssen et al., 2002; Sait et al., 2002; Joseph et al., 2003; Stevenson et al., 2004; da Rocha et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Some techniques mimic the conditions in situ by supplying extracts derived from the environment containing unspecified mixtures of macro- and micronutrients and other growth factors.
source: Other techniques mimic the conditions in situ in more detail by supplying extracts derived from the environment containing unspecified mixtures of macro- and micronutrients and other growth factors (Olsen and Bakken, 1987; Rappé et al., 2002; Zengler et al., 2002; Sipkema et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Providing direct contact with the environment proved highly productive in culturing species regarded as unculturable.
source: The most advanced development in this direction is to provide direct contact with the environment (Ben-Dov et al., 2009; Kaeberlein et al., 2002; Bollmann et al., 2007; Sizova et al., 2012), which proved highly productive in culturing species regarded as unculturable.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Miniaturization of culture vessels saves material and time while increasing throughput.
source: A complementary trend is the miniaturization of culture vessels to save material and time while increasing throughput (Zengler et al., 2002; Ben-Dov et al., 2009; Jiang et al., 2016a; Terekhov et al., 2017; Cao et al., 2017; Watterson et al., 2020; Villa et al., 2020; Martin et al., 2003; Ingham et al., 2007; Nichols et al., 2010; Gao et al., 2013; Jung et al., 2014; Ma et al., 2014a; Ma et al., 2014b; Tandogan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Miniaturization increases the chance of finding non-dormant, culturable variants of naturally occurring species as stochastic events.
source: Thereby, the chance of finding non-dormant, culturable variants of naturally occurring species, as stochastic events (Epstein, 2013), rises.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Epstein, 2013.

claim: Microscale culture techniques enable partitioning of complex bacterial communities at the single-cell level.
source: These microscale culture techniques enable partitioning of complex bacterial communities at the single-cell level, which allows various species to grow at their own speed without competition for space or nutrients.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the capabilities of microscale techniques, supported by citations in the preceding sentence.

claim: Single-cell partitioning allows various species to grow at their own speed without competition for space or nutrients.
source: These microscale culture techniques enable partitioning of complex bacterial communities at the single-cell level, which allows various species to grow at their own speed without competition for space or nutrients.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the benefits of single-cell partitioning.

claim: Microscale approaches can be divided into methods that arrange compartments into arrays and techniques that keep compartments mobile within the bulk population.
source: The reported microscale approaches can be divided into methods that arrange the compartments into arrays (Martin et al., 2003; Ingham et al., 2007; Nichols et al., 2010; Gao et al., 2013; Jung et al., 2014; Ma et al., 2014a; Ma et al., 2014b; Tandogan et al., 2014; Jiang et al., 2016a; Cao et al., 2017) and techniques that keep the compartments not fixed to positions but rather mobile within the bulk population (Zengler et al., 2002; Ben-Dov et al., 2009; Terekhov et al., 2017; Watterson et al., 2020; Villa et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature describing both types of approaches.

claim: The advantage of arrays is the possibility to address the same culture several times since the compartments are identified by their coordinates.
source: The clear advantage of arrays is the possibility to address the same culture several times since the compartments are identified by their coordinates.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the properties of array-based systems.

claim: Array technologies lose space by introducing distance between array positions and omitting expansion in the third dimension.
source: First, space is lost by introducing a distance between array positions and omitting the expansion in the third dimension.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the spatial limitations of 2D arrays.

claim: Fast automation is simpler with moving compartments than with arrays.
source: Second, fast automation is simpler with moving compartments and the continuous flow of compartments can be easily adjusted in speed and direction (Vincent et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Vincent et al., 2010.

claim: Without arrays, higher absolute numbers of compartments can be generated and processed per unit of time.
source: Consequently, without arrays, higher absolute numbers of compartments can be generated and processed per unit of time.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the preceding statements about automation advantages.

claim: Microfluidic droplets provide a genotype–phenotype linkage also for secreted products.
source: Microfluidic droplets provide a genotype–phenotype linkage also for secreted products, meaning that those compounds stay confined with the cell from which they originated.
evidence: This is established knowledge about droplet microfluidics properties.

claim: Secreted compounds stay confined with the cell from which they originated in microfluidic droplets.
source: Microfluidic droplets provide a genotype–phenotype linkage also for secreted products, meaning that those compounds stay confined with the cell from which they originated.
evidence: This is established knowledge about droplet compartmentalization.

claim: Droplets can be stored in bulk, allowing generation and incubation of large droplet populations under controlled aerobic conditions.
source: Droplets can be stored in bulk, allowing to generate and incubate large droplet populations under controlled aerobic conditions.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental methods described in the manuscript.

claim: A high-throughput screening for antimicrobial products using bacterial reporter strains in droplets was implemented.
source: Furthermore, we implemented a high-throughput screening for antimicrobial products using bacterial reporter strains in droplets (Mahler et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Mahler et al., 2018 and experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: The cultivation and screening strategy was verified by culturing a complex bacterial community derived from a soil sample.
source: We verified our cultivation and screening strategy by culturing a complex bacterial community derived from a soil sample in a growth substrate designed accordingly and compared the cultivation outcome to classical agar plate cultivation for the same sample.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented throughout the Results section.

claim: The cultivation outcome was compared to classical agar plate cultivation for the same sample.
source: We verified our cultivation and screening strategy by culturing a complex bacterial community derived from a soil sample in a growth substrate designed accordingly and compared the cultivation outcome to classical agar plate cultivation for the same sample.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 1-3.

claim: For one isolate that showed antimicrobial activity in the droplet screening, the secreted metabolites were identified and characterized.
source: For one of the isolates that showed antimicrobial activity in the droplet screening, we identified and characterized the secreted metabolites.
evidence: This is supported by LC-HRMS data and structural characterization in Figure 7.

claim: Cells were separated from each other by encapsulating them in droplets during droplet generation.
source: The workflow featured three major phases: first, cells were separated from each other by encapsulating them in droplets during droplet generation.
evidence: This describes the experimental workflow implemented in the study.

claim: All droplets were collected in a vessel where they lost their order.
source: All droplets were collected in a vessel, where they lost their order.
evidence: This describes the experimental workflow.

claim: Droplets in bulk were incubated together using dynamic droplet incubation, which ensured aerobic and homogenous cultivation conditions for months.
source: Second, droplets in bulk were incubated together using dynamic droplet incubation (Mahler et al., 2015), which ensured aerobic and homogenous cultivation conditions for months.
evidence: This is supported by the citation to Mahler et al., 2015 and experimental methods.

claim: Grown microbial cultures were isolated from droplets by depositing them on agar plates.
source: Third, grown microbial cultures were isolated from droplets by depositing them on agar plates.
evidence: This describes the experimental workflow shown in Figure 4.

claim: Either all droplets were deposited in an untargeted manner or droplets were first screened for antimicrobial activity and then only selected droplets were distributed on agar plates.
source: Either all droplets were deposited in an untargeted manner or droplets were first screened for antimicrobial activity and then only selected droplets were distributed on agar plates (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by the workflow diagram in Figure 1A and experimental data.

claim: The medium design followed the rationale of replicating the conditions in the natural environment as closely as possible.
source: For designing the medium in which single cells were encapsulated in droplets, we followed the rationale of replicating the conditions in the natural environment as closely as possible.
evidence: This describes the experimental design rationale.

claim: Low amounts of defined nutrients typically originating from plants were used, supplemented with cold-extracted soil extract and solid soil particles.
source: We used low amounts of defined nutrients typically originating from plants supplemented with a cold-extracted soil extract (CESE), prepared from the same soil that the community was derived from, and several solid soil particles (diameter <40 µm).
evidence: This describes the experimental medium composition.

claim: CESE contained dissolvable macro- and micronutrients and other effectors, like signaling molecules.
source: CESE contained dissolvable macro- and micronutrients and other effectors, like signaling molecules.
evidence: This is an inference about the composition of the soil extract.

claim: The number of cells occupying a droplet during an encapsulation event follows a Poisson distribution.
source: The number of cells occupying a droplet during an encapsulation event follows a Poisson distribution (Collins et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Collins et al., 2015.

claim: The concentration of cells at inoculation was adjusted to obtain not more than 30% occupied droplets (λ = 0.4, on average 0.4 cells/droplet).
source: As we aimed at one cell per droplet, we minimized the probability of several cells per droplet by adjusting the concentration of cells at inoculation to obtain not more than 30% occupied droplets (λ = 0.4, on average 0.4 cells/droplet).
evidence: This describes the experimental design parameters.

claim: The occurrence of several cells per droplet cannot be excluded due to a small statistical probability of 6.16% and biological reasons.
source: Nevertheless, the occurrence of several cells per droplet cannot be excluded due to a small statistical probability of 6.16% and biological reasons like cells adhering to the same soil particle or to each other.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on Poisson statistics and biological considerations.

claim: The droplets were stabilized by a biocompatible surfactant forming a monolayer at the aqueous/oil interphase.
source: The droplets were stabilized by a biocompatible surfactant forming a monolayer at the aqueous/oil interphase.
evidence: This describes the experimental method for droplet stabilization.

claim: The level of miniaturization (~200 pL droplet volume), in conjunction with bulk incubation, permitted droplet populations comprising on average 9 × 10^6 droplets.
source: The level of miniaturization (~200 pL droplet volume), in conjunction with bulk incubation, permitted droplet populations comprising on average 9 × 106 droplets.
evidence: This describes the experimental parameters achieved.

claim: The soil community was incubated with the same media composition at 20 °C for 28 days in both droplet and plate approaches.
source: The soil community was incubated with the same media composition at 20 °C for 28 days in both approaches.
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions for the comparison.

claim: After 28 days, the average occupation frequency of the eight droplet populations amounted to 22.4%, which translates into 3.03 × 10^6 CFU/mL.
source: After 28 days, the average occupation frequency of the eight populations amounted to 22.4%, which translates into 3.03 × 106 colony-forming units (CFUs)/mL (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data and calculations shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: On plates, the colony count is equivalent to 1.3 × 10^6 CFU/mL of the soil community.
source: On plates, the colony count is equivalent to 1.3 × 106 CFU/mL of the soil community.
evidence: This is supported by plate counting data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The more than twofold higher concentration of CFUs found during in-droplet cultivation indicates that the singularization and incubation of cells in droplets enabled more cells to replicate.
source: The more than twofold higher concentration of CFUs found during in-droplet cultivation indicates that the singularization and incubation of cells in droplets enabled more cells to replicate.
evidence: This is an inference based on the CFU data comparing droplets and plates.

claim: Uninformative operational taxonomic units (OTUs) were removed by a combination of a total count and prevalence filter resulting in 2106 final OTUs.
source: Uninformative operational taxonomic units (OTUs) were removed by a combination of a total count and prevalence filter resulting in 2106 final OTUs.
evidence: This describes the data analysis methods.

claim: Samples belonging to one sample type showed little dispersion, and plate and droplets-derived sample clusters did not overlap.
source: Samples belonging to one sample type showed little dispersion, and plate and droplets-derived sample clusters did not overlap.
evidence: This is supported by the PCoA analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: These results indicate clear dissimilarities between the cultivation outcome of the two methods but a reproducible community composition within one cultivation method.
source: These results indicate clear dissimilarities between the cultivation outcome of the two methods but a reproducible community composition within one cultivation method.
evidence: This is an inference based on the PCoA data in Figure 2A.

claim: The relative abundance of the phylum Actinobacteria among the cultivated species was more than twofold higher in droplets (37.9%) than on agar plates (15.7%).
source: The relative abundance of the phylum Actinobacteria among the cultivated species was more than twofold higher in droplets (37.9%) than on agar plates (15.7%).
evidence: This is supported by the community composition data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: More than 99% of reads in the Streptomyces-positive controls affiliated to Actinobacteria for both cultivation techniques.
source: As expected, more than 99% of reads in the Streptomyces-positive controls (Table 1) affiliated to Actinobacteria for both cultivation techniques, proving the absence of external contaminations.
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data and serves as a control validation.

claim: The composition of the extracted soil community was similar to the initial community structure of the original soil sample.
source: The composition of the extracted soil community was similar to the initial community structure of the original soil sample, indicating no technical bias of extracting the microbial cells from the soil matrix.
evidence: This is supported by the community composition data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The total number of OTUs, Good's Coverage, chao1, and Shannon indices were significantly higher in the droplet cultivation samples than in the plate cultivation samples.
source: The total number of OTUs, as well as Good's Coverage, chao1 (species richness) (Chao et al., 2006), and Shannon indices (species diversity) (Shannon, 1948) were significantly higher in the droplet cultivation samples than in the plate cultivation samples, suggesting a higher microbial diversity cultivated in droplets (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of alpha diversity indices shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The phylum Firmicutes showed significantly higher abundance on plates, comprising one-third of the community.
source: A pronounced distinction was the significantly higher abundance of the phylum Firmicutes on plates, comprising one-third of the community (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), while it was represented with only 5.3% in droplets.
evidence: This is supported by community composition data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: On plates, Firmicutes were mainly composed of five OTUs (three affiliating to Bacillus and two to Paenibacillus).
source: On plates, Firmicutes were mainly composed of five OTUs (three affiliating to Bacillus and two to Paenibacillus).
evidence: This is supported by taxonomic analysis of the sequencing data.

claim: Bacillus and Paenibacillus, together with Phyllobacterium, were the three most abundant genera on plates, accounting for 42% of all the sequences.
source: As expected, Bacillus and Paenibacillus, together with Phyllobacterium, were the three most abundant genera on plates, accounting for 42% of all the sequences (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by genus-level abundance data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Acinetobacter showed the highest relative abundance on the genus rank for droplets, accompanied by Agromyces and Micromonospora.
source: In contrast, Acinetobacter as a member of the γ-Proteobacteria showed the highest relative abundance on the genus rank for droplets, accompanied by Agromyces and Micromonospora.
evidence: This is supported by genus-level abundance data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Most taxa present on plates were also found in droplets, while many taxa were exclusively found in droplets but not on plates.
source: As a general trend, most taxa present on plates were also found in droplets, while many taxa were exclusively found in droplets but not on plates (Figure 3B, C, Figure 3—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claim: Among the taxa that were exclusively found in droplet samples, which accounted for almost 60% of all taxa, a considerable number of taxa were classified as uncultured at the genus level (151 taxa of 983 exclusive droplet taxa).
source: Among the taxa that were exclusively found in droplet samples, which accounted for almost 60% of all taxa, we found also a considerable number of taxa classified as uncultured at the genus level (151 taxa of 983 exclusive droplet taxa) (Figure 3—figure supplement 6B).
evidence: This is supported by taxonomic classification data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6B.

claim: 15.2% of the exclusive droplet taxa were classified as uncultured.
source: While 15.2% of the exclusive droplet taxa were classified as uncultured, only 1.2% of the taxa found in both approaches – droplet and plate – were classified as uncultured and 0% in exclusive plate taxa.
evidence: This is supported by taxonomic classification analysis.

claim: Only 1.2% of the taxa found in both approaches were classified as uncultured.
source: While 15.2% of the exclusive droplet taxa were classified as uncultured, only 1.2% of the taxa found in both approaches – droplet and plate – were classified as uncultured and 0% in exclusive plate taxa.
evidence: This is supported by taxonomic classification analysis.

claim: 0% of exclusive plate taxa were classified as uncultured.
source: While 15.2% of the exclusive droplet taxa were classified as uncultured, only 1.2% of the taxa found in both approaches – droplet and plate – were classified as uncultured and 0% in exclusive plate taxa.
evidence: This is supported by taxonomic classification analysis.

claim: Droplets were injected into a capillary at 10–50 droplets/s and guided to an agar plate mounted on a positioning system.
source: Droplets were injected into a capillary at 10–50 droplets/s and guided to an agar plate, mounted on a positioning system.
evidence: This describes the experimental setup shown in Figure 4.

claim: The plate was moved following a spiral pattern, leading to the distribution of droplets along the spiral streak over the agar plate.
source: While droplets and oil phase continuously emanated from the capillary tip, the plate was moved following a spiral pattern, leading to the distribution of droplets along the spiral streak over the agar plate.
evidence: This describes the experimental method shown in Figure 4.

claim: Both the volatile oil phase surrounding the droplets and the aqueous droplets evaporated fast, leaving behind the cells that were previously confined in droplets now spatially separated on the agar surface.
source: Both the volatile oil phase surrounding the droplets and, subsequently, also the aqueous droplets evaporated fast, leaving behind the cells that were previously confined in droplets now spatially separated on the agar surface.
evidence: This describes the physical process of droplet deposition.

claim: 224 colonies were picked after incubation of the plates.
source: We picked 224 colonies after incubation of the plates, trying to keep the selection random and thereby reflecting the true distribution of abundance for the bacterial diversity.
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure.

claim: In total, 301 axenic isolates were obtained on agar plates of which 266 were initially characterized by sequencing the full 16S rRNA gene.
source: In total, 301 axenic isolates were obtained on agar plates of which 266 were initially characterized by sequencing the full 16S rRNA gene.
evidence: This describes the experimental results.

claim: The isolates covered four major phyla resolving in 11 different genera.
source: The isolates covered four major phyla resolving in 11 different genera (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by taxonomic classification data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Most of the isolates were classified as Bacillus (52.3%).
source: Most of the isolates were classified as Bacillus (52.3%), underlining the strong bias towards Firmicutes caused by intermediate cultivation on agar plates.
evidence: This is supported by taxonomic classification data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The accumulated abundance of Actinobacteria amounted to 30.5%, resembling the abundance in the droplet amplicon data.
source: Nevertheless, the accumulated abundance of Actinobacteria amounted to 30.5%, resembling the abundance in the droplet amplicon data.
evidence: This is supported by taxonomic classification data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The Actinobacteria were represented by several rarely observed genera like Kocuria and Leifsonia.
source: Moreover, the Actinobacteria were represented by several rarely observed genera like Kocuria and Leifsonia, and a notable high frequency of Micromonospora with 22.9%, which showcases the influence of in-droplet cultivation.
evidence: This is supported by taxonomic classification data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Micromonospora showed a notable high frequency of 22.9%.
source: Moreover, the Actinobacteria were represented by several rarely observed genera like Kocuria and Leifsonia, and a notable high frequency of Micromonospora with 22.9%, which showcases the influence of in-droplet cultivation.
evidence: This is supported by taxonomic classification data shown in Figure 5.

claim: One of the isolates clustered only to reference sequences of uncultured bacteria assigned to the family Cytophagaceae.
source: Remarkably, one of the isolates clustered only to reference sequences of uncultured bacteria assigned to the family Cytophagaceae.
evidence: This is supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The uncultured Cytophagaceae isolate could not be maintained for long on standard agar plates.
source: However, this isolate could not be maintained for long on standard agar plates.
evidence: This is an observation from the cultivation experiments.

claim: Cells of a reporter strain were picoinjected into all droplets of a population after 1 month incubation.
source: For this purpose, we picoinjected cells of a reporter strain into all droplets of a population after 1 month incubation (Video 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure shown in Video 1.

claim: Droplets with inhibited reporter cells (low red fluorescence signals) were selected in a droplet sorting operation on-chip.
source: Based on the fluorescent signal, droplets with inhibited reporter cells (low red fluorescence signals) were selected in a droplet sorting operation on-chip (Video 2) and subsequently distributed on agar plates to recover soil bacteria-producing antimicrobial compounds.
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure shown in Video 2.

claim: Four different screening experiments explored combinations of two different reporter strains (E. coli and B. subtilis) and two different media.
source: In four different screening experiments, we explored combinations of two different reporter strains, Escherichia coli and Bacillus subtilis, as representatives of Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, and two different media to cultivate the soil community in droplets (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: Among the inhibiting isolates, an enrichment of Actinobacteria and Alphaproteobacteria represented by various genera like Kocuria, Microbacterium, and Sphingomonas was observed for the B. subtilis reporter.
source: We observed among the inhibiting isolates an enrichment of Actinobacteria and Alphaproteobacteria represented by various genera like Kocuria, Microbacterium, and Sphingomonas for the B. subtilis reporter (Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by taxonomic classification data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The spectrum of genera recovered with the E. coli reporter was broader.
source: In contrast, the spectrum of genera recovered with the E. coli reporter was broader.
evidence: This is supported by taxonomic classification data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The most abundant genus for both reporters was Bacillus sp.
source: The most abundant genus for both reporters was, however, Bacillus sp. .
evidence: This is supported by taxonomic classification data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Two isolates falling in the Cytophagaceae family but being only distantly related to known type strains (<95%) were obtained.
source: Interestingly, two isolates falling in the Cytophagaceae family but being only distantly related to known type strains (<95%) were obtained.
evidence: This is supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The two Cytophagaceae isolates from screening did not cluster closely to the previously uncultivated Cytophagaceae isolate gained in the untargeted isolation.
source: They also did not cluster closely to the previously uncultivated Cytophagaceae isolate gained in the untargeted isolation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), indicating that those isolates represent an additional new strain.
evidence: This is supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Cytophagaceae isolates from screening could not be maintained on agar plates for long.
source: As before, these isolates could not be maintained on agar plates for long.
evidence: This is an observation from the cultivation experiments.

claim: Isolate D121-0906-b3-2-1 is closely related to Bacillus tequilensis (99.79%).
source: This isolate (D121-0906-b3-2-1) is closely related to Bacillus tequilensis (99.79%) and was isolated using B. subtilis as reporter strain in droplets.
evidence: This is supported by 16S rRNA gene sequence analysis.

claim: Isolate D121-0906-b3-2-1 showed a peculiar increase in growth rate when challenged with M. vaccae.
source: When challenged with M. vaccae, isolate D121-0906-b3-2-1 showed a peculiar increase in growth rate (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by bioactivity assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The isolate's crude culture supernatant exhibited a strong antifungal activity against test strains like Candida albicans, Sporobolomyces salmonicolor, and Penicillium notatum.
source: Additionally, the isolates' crude culture supernatant exhibited a strong antifungal activity against test strains like Candida albicans, Sporobolomyces salmonicolor, and Penicillium notatum (Supplementary file 1—table 2).
evidence: This is supported by bioactivity assay data in Supplementary file 1—table 2.

claim: Bacillus sp. D121-0906-b3-2-1 was cultured under several conditions including varying media composition and duration of cultivation.
source: For increasing the production titer of the natural products, we cultured Bacillus sp. D121-0906-b3-2-1 under several conditions including varying media composition and duration of cultivation (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach for metabolite production.

claim: Extraction took place with either ethyl acetate or the absorber resin XAD-2.
source: In addition, extraction took place with either ethyl acetate or the absorber resin XAD-2.
evidence: This describes the experimental methods.

claim: Five compounds were detected in the extracts by LC-HRMS.
source: The extracts were analyzed by liquid chromatography coupled to high resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) and five compounds were detected.
evidence: This is supported by LC-HRMS data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Compounds 1 and 2 are identical with bacillaene A and B, known strong antibacterial polyketides.
source: The predicted molecular formulas as well as a characteristic UV absorption spectrum indicated that 1 and 2 are identical with bacillaene A and B, known strong antibacterial polyketides active against a variety of strains (Patel et al., 1995; Müller et al., 2014; Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 4A, B).
evidence: This is supported by LC-HRMS data, UV spectra, and MS/MS fragmentation patterns shown in Figure 7 and Figure 7—figure supplement 4, along with citations to published literature.

claim: Tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) fragmentation analysis confirmed the identification of bacillaenes.
source: Tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) fragmentation analysis confirmed this assumption.
evidence: This is supported by MS/MS data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 4.

claim: Three highly lipophilic metabolites (3–5) were detected in the extracts of Bacillus sp. D121-0906-b3-2-1.
source: Furthermore, we detected three highly lipophilic metabolites (3–5) in the extracts of Bacillus sp. D121-0906-b3-2-1 with molecular masses of m/z 1006 [M–H]– (3), m/z 1020 [M–H]– (4), and m/z 1034 [M–H]– (5), respectively.
evidence: This is supported by LC-HRMS data shown in Figure 7.

claim: High-resolution MS data and MS/MS analysis revealed these cryptic molecules to be surfactins, cytotoxic lipopeptides.
source: High-resolution MS data, as well as characteristic amino acid fragments obtained from HRESI-MS/MS analysis, revealed these cryptic molecules to be surfactins (3–5), cytotoxic lipopeptides (Figure 7C, Figure 7—figure supplement 5D–F; Kakinuma et al., 1969; Bonmatin et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by LC-HRMS and MS/MS data shown in Figure 7 and Figure 7—figure supplement 5, along with citations to published literature.

claim: The retention times of a surfactin standard were identical with compound 3.
source: The retention times of a surfactin standard (Merck) were identical with 3 (Figure 7—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This is supported by LC-HRMS comparison data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 5A.

claim: A mass shift of +18 Da was observed after adding base to the extracts, confirming a cyclized form of the lipopeptides.
source: To exclude a linearized form of the surfactins, called gageostatins (Tareq et al., 2014), we added base (0.4 M NaOH) to the extracts to cleave the ester bond of 3. A mass shift of +18 Da was observed, confirming a cyclized form of the lipopeptides (Figure 7—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: This is supported by MS data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 5C and a citation to Tareq et al., 2014.

claim: Surfactins and surfactin-like natural products are known to exert a broad spectrum of antimicrobial effects against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria as well as fungi.
source: Surfactins and surfactin-like natural products are known to exert a broad spectrum of antimicrobial effects against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria as well as fungi (Vitullo et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2012; Luo et al., 2015; Jiang et al., 2016b) and may thus explain the strong antimicrobial effects of the Bacillus sp. extracts towards the test strain panel.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The bacillaene fraction inhibited growth of B. subtilis most effectively while the surfactin fractions showed weaker antibacterial activities.
source: The bacillaene fraction inhibited growth of B. subtilis most effectively while the surfactin fractions showed weaker antibacterial activities.
evidence: This is supported by agar diffusion assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3.

claim: The droplet cultivation method attains a 180-fold higher number of droplets than the microfluidic streak plate.
source: Thereby, we attain a 180-fold higher number of droplets and a higher cultivation density than the microfluidic streak plate (Jiang et al., 2016a), for instance (50.000 × 180 pL droplets in an array).
evidence: This is a comparison calculation based on the citation to Jiang et al., 2016a.

claim: The method does not suffer from cross-contamination of cells between the compartments or compartment and continuous phase, in contrast to systems relying on agarose-stabilized gel microdroplets.
source: In contrast to systems relying on agarose-stabilized gel microdroplets incubated in aqueous medium (Zengler et al., 2002; Akselband et al., 2006), our method does not suffer from cross-contamination of cells between the compartments or compartment and continuous phase.
evidence: This is a comparison to other methods cited in the literature.

claim: The screening protocol is not feasible when double emulsions or gel-stabilized droplets are used.
source: Such a protocol is not feasible when double emulsions (Terekhov et al., 2017) or gel-stabilized droplets are used.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of other methods, supported by a citation.

claim: A more diverse subset of cultured bacteria and a twofold higher CFU concentration compared to plates have presumably been achieved for three reasons: absence of competition in single-cell confinement, the high number of incubated cells, and the new and unique cultivation conditions in droplets during long-term dynamic droplet incubation.
source: A more diverse subset of cultured bacteria and a twofold higher CFU concentration compared to plates have presumably been achieved for three reasons: (i) absence of competition in single-cell confinement, (ii) the high number of incubated cells, and (iii) the new and unique cultivation conditions in our droplets during long-term dynamic droplet incubation.
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanisms underlying the observed results.

claim: Conditions like low nutrient amounts and long incubation times might favor growth and metabolic activity of slow growing species over fast growing species.
source: We also specifically chose conditions like low nutrient amounts and long incubation times that might favor growth and metabolic activity of slow growing species over fast growing species.
evidence: This is a speculation about the effects of the chosen cultivation conditions.

claim: Fast growing species are usually readily culturable and have been extensively screened in standard natural product screenings.
source: We installed this bias towards slow growing species in our screening as a dereplication strategy because fast growing species are usually readily culturable and have been extensively screened in standard natural product screenings.
evidence: This is established knowledge in natural product discovery.

claim: Only a few molecules with relatively high partitioning coefficients, meaning fairly hydrophobic compounds, might leak into the oil.
source: In general, only a few molecules with relatively high partitioning coefficients, meaning fairly hydrophobic compounds, might leak into the oil (Skhiri et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Skhiri et al., 2012.

claim: Molecules which are usually poorly soluble in the perfluorinated continuous phase can only partition into the continuous phase mediated by excessive surfactant molecules.
source: Other molecules, which are usually poorly soluble in the perfluorinated continuous phase, can only partition into the continuous phase mediated by excessive surfactant molecules, unbound to the droplet border (Gruner et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Gruner et al., 2016.

claim: Interdroplet transport can be minimized by decreasing surfactant concentrations.
source: This kind of interdroplet transport can be minimized by decreasing surfactant concentrations, as was done here.
evidence: This is supported by the citation to Gruner et al., 2016 and the experimental design.

claim: The risk for chemical cross-talk is low.
source: Although the risk for chemical cross-talk is low, it could be problematic for the detection of antibiotics.
evidence: This is an inference based on the properties of the droplet system.

claim: The risk to miss antibiotics is higher for hydrophobic compounds, making the system favor the detection of hydrophilic substances.
source: Overall, the risk to miss antibiotics is higher for hydrophobic compounds, making the system favor the detection of hydrophilic substances.
evidence: This is an inference about the screening bias of the system.

claim: The outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria makes them more resistant to a number of hydrophobic antimicrobials.
source: We understand the focus on hydrophilic antibiotics as a strength since the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria, including many clinically relevant pathogens, makes them more resistant to a number of hydrophobic antimicrobials (Savage, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Savage, 2001.

claim: Allowing communication between species might preserve to some extent the growth-stimulating influence of multispecies communities.
source: Allowing communication between species might preserve to some extent the growth-stimulating influence of multispecies communities.
evidence: This is a speculation about a potential benefit of interdroplet transport.

claim: The yield of unusual isolates could be further increased by solely focusing on exceptional morphologies during colony picking.
source: Presumably, the yield of unusual isolates could be further increased by solely focusing on exceptional morphologies during colony picking.
evidence: This is a speculation about how to improve the method.

claim: The overall taxonomic distribution found after in-droplet cultivation could not be recovered with the droplet depositioning and isolation procedure on agar plates.
source: Nevertheless, the overall taxonomic distribution found after in-droplet cultivation could not be recovered with our droplet depositioning and isolation procedure on agar plates.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the amplicon data to the isolate data.

claim: The isolate collection was biased by organisms abundantly found on solid media plates.
source: The isolate collection was biased by organisms abundantly found on solid media plates and a number of species able to grow in droplets could not be recovered.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed taxonomic distributions.

claim: Large differences in culturability for several known strains and isolation campaigns have been described depending on the choice of liquid or solid cultivation media.
source: Large differences in culturability for several known strains and isolation campaigns have been described depending on the choice of liquid or solid cultivation media (Nosho et al., 2018; Shigematsu et al., 2007; Wai et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The change from liquid to solid cultivation contributed to the loss of some isolates.
source: Hence, it can be assumed that this is the case also for many so far unknown species. We, therefore, hypothesize that the change from liquid to solid cultivation contributed to the loss of some isolates, which could not be maintained in culture for extended periods outside of droplets.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the cited literature and observations.

claim: The high parallelization in droplet cultivation leads to substantially increased chances to find rare scout cells.
source: The high parallelization in droplet cultivation leads to substantially increased chances to find rare scout cells, which can replicate and turn into culturable variants (spontaneous domestication).
evidence: This is an inference based on the scout model theory mentioned earlier.

claim: Domesticated variants would subsequently also grow on agar plates and become accessible within the droplet workflow.
source: Those domesticated variants would subsequently also grow on agar plates and become accessible within our droplet workflow.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of strain recovery.

claim: The method assists in strain prioritization during genome mining or guides future isolation campaigns even when axenic cultures cannot be maintained.
source: Even though axenic cultures of putative new species could not be maintained with standard microbiological cultivation after isolation from droplets, the cells could be used for obtaining high-quality genome information. Thereby, our method assists in strain prioritization during genome mining or guide future isolation campaigns.
evidence: This is an inference about the utility of the method.

claim: Cloning and heterologous expression of unusual biosynthetic gene clusters might pave the way for identifying novel antibiotics that would have otherwise stayed undetected.
source: Additionally, cloning and heterologous expression of unusual biosynthetic gene clusters with non-canonical domain architectures might pave the way for identifying novel antibiotics that would have otherwise stayed undetected.
evidence: This is a speculation about future applications.

claim: Charging the perfluorinated oil with nitrogen or other gases during dynamic droplet incubation could enable microaerophilic or even anaerobic incubation.
source: To further increase the number of rare taxa cultivated in droplets, we could charge the perfluorinated oil carrying dissolved gases with nitrogen or other gases during dynamic droplet incubation. Thereby, a microaerophilic or even anaerobic incubation would be enabled, which was recently shown to dramatically increase the species richness in droplets for human microbiomes (Watterson et al., 2020; Villa et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a speculation about future improvements, supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: Anaerobic incubation was recently shown to dramatically increase the species richness in droplets for human microbiomes.
source: Thereby, a microaerophilic or even anaerobic incubation would be enabled, which was recently shown to dramatically increase the species richness in droplets for human microbiomes (Watterson et al., 2020; Villa et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Watterson et al., 2020 and Villa et al., 2020.

claim: Encapsulating several cells per droplet could create simplified multispecies communities, which have the potential to either support growth of dependent species or to exert a change in natural product biosynthesis.
source: Besides encapsulating single cells, several cells could be confined per droplet creating simplified multispecies communities, which have the potential to either support growth of dependent species (Tanaka and Benno, 2015) or to exert a change in natural product biosynthesis (Shi et al., 2017; Molloy and Hertweck, 2017).
evidence: This is a speculation about future applications, supported by citations to published literature.

claim: By passaging a community several times through the in-droplet cultivation, replicating organisms become enriched, and the chance of strain domestication increases.
source: Furthermore, we here have isolated strains after one incubation round in droplets, but alternatively the emulsion can be broken under controlled conditions and a new droplet cultivation can be started from the pooled cell suspension. By passaging a community several times through the in-droplet cultivation, replicating organisms become enriched, and the chance of strain domestication increases (Bollmann et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a speculation about future improvements, supported by a citation to Bollmann et al., 2007.

claim: The cultivation and screening strategy is comprehensive and adaptable to the challenging needs of fastidious microorganisms representing interesting sources for natural products.
source: Our cultivation and screening strategy has proven to be comprehensive and adaptable to the challenging needs of fastidious microorganisms representing interesting sources for natural products.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental results presented.

claim: The bacterial diversity of numerous natural habitats will be explored in more depth with this strategy.
source: Therefore, we envision that the bacterial diversity of numerous natural habitats, especially including environments with limited access to samples (e.g., patient biopsies), will be explored in more depth with our strategy.
evidence: This is a speculation about future applications.

claim: The combination of bacterial strain discovery during in-droplet cultivation with subsequent selection through a reporter assay will streamline efforts towards new scaffold structures for antibiotic development.
source: The combination of bacterial strain discovery during the in-droplet cultivation phase with subsequent selection of the most auspicious candidates for natural product biosynthesis through a highly robust reporter assay will streamline our efforts towards new scaffold structures for the development of antibiotics.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the potential impact of the method.
